title: Tractors & Trailers
strapline: Hitch up the trailer, load the harvest, and rumble round the farm delivering the goods.
intent: Children explore how a tractor pulls a load — hitching, towing and feeling how much harder a full trailer is to move.
Children load, count and share cargo: bales, vegetables, animals, sacks of feed.
Children connect the play to real farm work and where food comes from.
Children use transporting and connecting schemas with vehicles built to carry and couple.
Children cooperate to run the farm — one drives, one loads, one opens the gate.
implementation: Provide tractors and trailers that really hitch and unhitch, plus loose 'cargo' — corks, pom-poms, small animals, stones.
Let children feel the difference an empty and a full trailer make, and talk about heavy and light.
Set up farm jobs with a purpose: collect the harvest, deliver hay to the animals, take the milk to the shop.
Feed in the maths — count the bales on, share them between two fields, notice which trailer holds more.
Model the coupling talk — 'hitch it on, load it up, off to the barn' — and the connecting schema at work.
Add gates that open and close, ramps and a muddy track for the tractors to churn along.
Talk about real farms, tractors children have seen, and how our food is grown and gathered.
key_questions: Is the trailer harder to pull when it's full or empty?
How many bales can you fit on before they fall off?
Where does this load need to go on the farm?
How will you hitch the trailer onto the tractor?
How could we share the vegetables between the two fields?

impact.text: Children hitch, tow and transport loads, feeding a connecting and transporting schema.
Children count and share cargo and compare which trailer holds more.
Children feel and talk about heavy and light as the trailer fills and empties.
Children talk about real farms and where our food comes from.
Children run the farm together — driving, loading, opening gates — in cooperative play.
Children couple and uncouple trailers with careful, controlled fingers.

enhancements: Tractors and trailers that genuinely hitch and unhitch.
Loose cargo — corks, pom-poms, pebbles, small animals, mini hay bales.
A farm layout with fields, a barn, gates that open and a muddy track.
A weighing station to compare full and empty trailers.
Sacks, buckets and a loading ramp for the harvest.
Pictures of real tractors at work through the seasons.
A delivery board: which field needs hay, which needs seed?

playing_exploring: Children explore towing and loading, testing how much the trailer will hold.
They replay farm scenes they've seen and imagine the rest.
active_learning: Children keep loading and delivering until every field is done.
They work at the tricky hitch until the trailer couples on.
creating_thinking: Children solve how to balance the load and share it out fairly.
They plan the deliveries and adapt when the trailer tips.
